facts.title: Country and period
facts.text: Country: South Africa (ZAF). Annual period 2014–2025, monthly series 2014-01-01 → 2025-12-01. Levels: ADM1, ADM2. Synthetic data: no.

facts.title: National trend
facts.text: Between 2014 and 2025, night-time light in South Africa changed by +2.1% per year (95% CI: +0.6% to +3.0%). Over the last 12 months, the seasonally adjusted level is +3.0% relative to the previous 12 months. (confidence high: significant trend (p < 0.01; n = 12))

facts.title: Regions
facts.text: Of 52 ADM2 units, 33 show significant growth, 16 are stagnating and 3 are declining. Light remains concentrated: Gauteng accounts for 20% of national light. (confidence medium: classification of 52 units, threshold ±1%/yr and p < 0.10)

facts.title: Convergence
facts.text: Across ADM2 units, light per capita converges: the least-lit units are catching up. (confidence medium: β = −0.064 [−0.084; −0.045], n = 52)

facts.title: Link with GDP
facts.text: The elasticity of light with respect to real GDP is 1.96 in levels (95% CI: −0.19 to 4.11, R² = 0.36, 12 years) and −0.27 in growth rates (CI: −0.98 to 0.45). Out of sample, light growth tracks GDP growth with a correlation of −0.54 (mean absolute error: 1.7 percentage points of growth). (confidence medium: n = 12, significant but wide CI (4.31))

facts.title: Shocks
facts.text: The most pronounced shock in the seasonally adjusted series is “COVID-19”: trough of -10.4% (09/2020), return to the pre-shock level after 7 months. (confidence low: trough compared with pre-shock month-to-month variability)

facts.title: Inequality and access
facts.text: The Gini coefficient of light per capita (ADM2) is 0.23 in 2025 (no significant change since 2014). About 0.50 million people live in inhabited areas with no detectable light (18% of the inhabited population). (confidence medium: sensitive to the radiance threshold (from 0.50 to 0.54 M depending on the threshold); a proxy for outdoor lighting, not for grid connection)

facts.title: Industrial zones
facts.text: 400 industrial clusters detected from concordant satellite signals: 40 heavy industry, 77 business parks & logistics, 221 oil & gas sites and 62 isolated sites to verify. They emit 22.3% of national light (latest year); their light changes by -1.4% per year. Gauteng has the most industrial activity. (confidence low: no reference list available to validate the detection)

facts.title: Summer tourism
facts.text: 1 of 52 units show a net summer light excess of at least 10%: City of Cape Town (Western Cape). The median net excess reaches +13% in the most touristic zone. The season index (base 100 = 2019) falls to 103 in 2020 and stands at 41 in 2025. (confidence low: correlation of -0.28 with international tourist arrivals (WDI) (7 years))

facts.title: Urbanisation
facts.text: The lit area changes by +6.8% per year, against +1.0% for population. Of 52 ADM2 units: 45 show electrified urbanisation, 2 balanced growth, 3 unlit growth. Between 2014 and 2025, 51,243 km² became lit, of which 1,415 km² in already inhabited areas (≈ 49k newly lit inhabitants). Largest expansion: O.R.Tambo (Eastern Cape), Sekhukhune (Limpopo), Capricorn (Limpopo). (confidence high: rank correlation of 0.80 with GHSL built-up growth (52 units))

facts.title: Key indicators
facts.text: Annual growth of light = +2.1% (2014–2025, robust slope (Theil–Sen)); Last 12 months vs previous 12 = +3.0% (seasonally adjusted series, up to 12/2025); Light–GDP elasticity = 1.96 (95% CI −0.19 to 4.11 · confidence medium); Gini of light per capita = 0.23 (ADM2 units, 2025); People in the dark = 0.50 M (18% of the inhabited population, 2025); Share of the top region = 20% (Gauteng, 2025); Industrial clusters = 400 (22% of national light); Tourist zones = 1 (max. summer excess +13% (City of Cape Town (Western Cape))); Lit area = +6.8% (annual growth; population +1.0%/yr)

facts.title: Recommendations
facts.text: • Use night-time lights as a leading and subnational indicator, as a complement to — never a replacement for — the national accounts. • Publish regional GDP estimates as experimental statistics, with intervals and a methodological note, after comparison with available regional accounts. • Cross-check the map of populations “in the dark” against grid-connection registers: the average gap with the World Bank access rate is -6 percentage points. • Document breaks detected without an associated event (sensor change, outage, local event) before any economic interpretation. • Have the 62 isolated sites checked on high-resolution imagery and complete the official register of industrial zones used as the validation reference. • Monitor the light of industrial clusters monthly as a leading indicator of industrial output, and compare it with the industrial production index where one exists. • Publish the tourist season index right after the summer (VIIRS data are available within weeks), ahead of hotel-night statistics, and recalibrate it on them every year. • Cross newly lit areas with urban plans and grid-connection registers to tell planned expansion, informal settlements and rural electrification apart. • Prioritise infrastructure (power grid, services) where population grows faster than the lit area: City of Cape Town (Western Cape), City of Johannesburg (Gauteng), Ekurhuleni (Gauteng). • Update the dashboard every quarter (monthly VIIRS series) and every year (annual VNL composites).

facts.title: Limitation: What lights measure
facts.text: Upward radiance emitted around 01:30: agriculture, daytime trade, poorly lit services and the rural informal economy are poorly captured.

facts.title: Limitation: Saturation and blooming
facts.text: DMSP saturates in city centres (DN 63) and “blooms” beyond lit areas; VIIRS is much better, but blooming still inflates the lit area of cities.

facts.title: Limitation: Gas flares and isolated sites
facts.text: The automatic mask may remove isolated mines, ports or power plants, and miss small flares; candidates are exported for verification.

facts.title: Limitation: Clouds, seasons, moon
facts.text: Cloudy months are only partially observed; STL removes average seasonality but not an abnormal season (snow, late monsoon).

facts.title: Limitation: Product breaks
facts.text: DMSP and VIIRS are not directly comparable: the harmonised long series (Li et al., 2020) is a modelled product, to be read for trends only.

facts.title: Limitation: NTL–GDP elasticity
facts.text: Estimated on 10 to 30 annual observations: wide intervals, possible instability, a non-causal relationship that varies with the level of development.

facts.title: Limitation: Access to electricity
facts.text: “Inhabited without light” ≠ “not connected”: a connected household with low consumption is invisible; the indicator depends strongly on the radiance threshold and the population data.

facts.title: Limitation: Administrative boundaries
facts.text: geoBoundaries/GAUL may differ from official boundaries; small ADM2 units are sensitive to light spilling over from neighbouring units.

facts.title: Limitation: Industrial zones
facts.text: Detection relies on thresholds: a power plant, a port or a large shopping centre can meet the signals; a dimly lit factory without visible emissions is missed. Sentinel-5P (≈ 5 km) and MODIS (1 km) are coarser than VIIRS: NO₂/SO₂/heat signals describe a neighbourhood, not a building.

facts.title: Limitation: Summer tourism
facts.text: The summer excess captures any rise in summer light (second homes, diaspora visits, festivals, construction), not only tourism; at high latitudes, very short summer nights reduce VIIRS observations. Ramadan changes night-time activity: the summers concerned are flagged.

facts.title: Limitation: Urbanisation
facts.text: The lit area depends on the detection threshold and on light blooming around cities; a connected but dimly lit neighbourhood stays invisible. Population (GHSL/WorldPop) is modelled from censuses: its growth is not an independent observation, and years between two epochs are interpolated.

facts.title: ADM2: ranking
facts.text: 52 ADM2 units. Classes: Growth 33, Stagnation 16, Decline 3. Fastest growth: Alfred Nzo (Eastern Cape) (+17.2%), Umkhanyakude (KwaZulu-Natal) (+16.0%), O.R.Tambo (Eastern Cape) (+12.2%), Umzinyathi (KwaZulu-Natal) (+9.6%), iLembe (KwaZulu-Natal) (+6.9%), Amathole (Eastern Cape) (+6.4%), Uthukela (KwaZulu-Natal) (+6.2%), Sisonke (KwaZulu-Natal) (+6.1%). Slowest: Nelson Mandela Bay (Eastern Cape) (-2.6%), Xhariep (Free State) (-1.9%), City of Johannesburg (Gauteng) (-1.7%), City of Cape Town (Western Cape) (-1.3%), Buffalo City (Eastern Cape) (-1.1%), Ekurhuleni (Gauteng) (-1.0%), Lejweleputswa (Free State) (-0.4%), City of Tshwane (Gauteng) (-0.4%).

facts.title: ADM2: brightest
facts.text: Brightest units: City of Tshwane (Gauteng) (5.9%), City of Johannesburg (Gauteng) (5.5%), eThekwini (KwaZulu-Natal) (4.9%), Bojanala (North West) (4.8%), Ehlanzeni (Mpumalanga) (4.4%), Nkangala (Mpumalanga) (4.2%), Ekurhuleni (Gauteng) (3.9%), City of Cape Town (Western Cape) (3.8%), Sekhukhune (Limpopo) (3.2%), Mopani (Limpopo) (2.9%).

facts.title: Convergence and concentration
facts.text: β-convergence (ADM2): β = -0.064 (CI -0.084 to -0.045, n = 52). β < 0 with a fully negative CI = convergence. Share of the leading region: 27.0% in 2014 → 19.9% in 2025; HHI 0.133.

facts.title: Elasticity (levels)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in levels: β = 1.96 (95% CI -0.19 to 4.11, R² = 0.36, n = 12, confidence medium: n = 12, significant but wide CI (4.31)). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Elasticity (growth rates)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in growth rates: β = -0.27 (95% CI -0.98 to 0.45, R² = 0.01, n = 11, confidence low: n = 11, not significant (p = 0.47)). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Elasticity (long DMSP–VIIRS series)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in long DMSP–VIIRS series: β = 0.87 (95% CI 0.58 to 1.15, R² = 0.88, n = 30, confidence high: n = 30, p < 0.01, narrow CI). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Out-of-sample tracking
facts.text: Out of sample, light-based growth has a correlation of -0.54 with official growth; mean absolute error 1.7 percentage point.

facts.title: Shock: COVID-19
facts.text: COVID-19 (2020-03-01 → 2021-06-30): trough of -10.4% on 2020-09-01, back to the pre-shock level after 7 months. Distinguishable from noise: no.

facts.title: Detected breaks
facts.text: Structural breaks: 2017-02-01 (11.8 %); 2022-07-01 (-13.3 %); 2024-07-01 (8.6 %). Without a known event within ±6 months: 3.

facts.title: Regional impact of shocks
facts.text: Hardest-hit regions (trough): Western Cape -18.7 % (covid19), Mpumalanga -15.5 % (covid19), Gauteng -15.2 % (covid19), Free State -14.2 % (covid19), North West -13.8 % (covid19).

facts.title: Gini and Theil
facts.text: Gini of light per capita (ADM2): 0.226 in 2014 → 0.229 in 2025 (change 0.003, bootstrap CI -0.086 to 0.064). Theil T 0.082; between-region share 50%.

facts.title: Population in the dark
facts.text: People in inhabited areas without detectable light: 0.48 M (20%) in 2014 → 0.50 M (18%) in 2025. Urban/rural light-per-capita ratio 0.3. Proxy of electricity access, sensitive to the threshold.

facts.title: Comparison with the World Bank
facts.text: Average gap between the share of people in lit areas and the World Bank electricity-access rate: -5.6 points.

facts.title: Industrial zones: summary
facts.text: 400 industrial clusters (≥ 3 of 6 signals): Oil, gas & flares 221, Business park & logistics 77, Isolated site to verify 62, Heavy industry 40. Share of national light: 22.3%; annual growth -1.4%. No validation available.

facts.title: Main industrial clusters
facts.text: IND-001 — Oil, gas & flares in City of Johannesburg (Gauteng) (3252.52 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-004 — Oil, gas & flares in Gert Sibande (Mpumalanga) (155.875 km², 4 signals, confidence medium); IND-002 — Oil, gas & flares in Sedibeng (Gauteng) (204.035 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-003 — Oil, gas & flares in Nkangala (Mpumalanga) (179.31 km², 4 signals, confidence medium); IND-006 — Oil, gas & flares in Nkangala (Mpumalanga) (113.52 km², 4 signals, confidence medium); IND-005 — Isolated site to verify in Sedibeng (Gauteng) (133.3 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-015 — Oil, gas & flares in City of Cape Town (Western Cape) (22.36 km², 2 signals, confidence low); IND-018 — Oil, gas & flares in Fezile Dabi (Free State) (15.695 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-032 — Oil, gas & flares in City of Cape Town (Western Cape) (10.32 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-008 — Heavy industry in Sedibeng (Gauteng) (40.85 km², 4 signals, confidence medium)

facts.text: Correlation between the growth of industrial light and of industry value added (World Bank, NV.IND.TOTL.KD): 0.23 over 11 years.

facts.title: Tourism: tourist zones
facts.text: 1 tourist zone(s) out of 52 ADM2 units (net summer excess ≥ 10%, peak months [12, 1]): City of Cape Town (Western Cape) (+13%, confidence high).

facts.title: Validation with hotel nights
facts.text: Correlation between the season index and international tourist arrivals (WDI): -0.28 (7 years; in growth rates: 0.13).

facts.title: Urbanisation: lit area and population
facts.text: National lit area: +6.8% per year; population: +1.0% per year. Classes (ADM2): Electrified urbanisation 45, Unlit growth 3, Balanced growth 2, Stable or declining 2.

facts.title: Urbanisation: newly lit areas
facts.text: Between 2014 and 2025: 51,243 km² newly lit, of which 1,415 km² already inhabited (electrification, ≈ 49k people) and 49,828 km² of new settlements; 1,756 km² lost their light.

facts.title: Urbanisation: units
facts.text: Fastest lit-area expansion: Alfred Nzo (Eastern Cape) (+23.7%/yr), O.R.Tambo (Eastern Cape) (+21.2%/yr), Umkhanyakude (KwaZulu-Natal) (+19.2%/yr), Umzinyathi (KwaZulu-Natal) (+18.7%/yr), Amathole (Eastern Cape) (+17.3%/yr), Joe Gqabi (Eastern Cape) (+13.4%/yr). Unlit growth (population faster than light): City of Cape Town (Western Cape), City of Johannesburg (Gauteng), Ekurhuleni (Gauteng).

facts.title: Validation with GHSL built-up
facts.text: Spearman rank correlation between lit-area growth and GHSL built-up growth: 0.80 (p = 0.000, 52 units).

facts.title: Quality and international standards
facts.text: Night-time-light indicators are experimental statistics: they complement official statistics and do not replace them. Every output is published with its method, validation, uncertainty, limitations and a confidence level. Frameworks applied: UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics, DQAF, UNECE GSBPM, FAIR principles.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Time dynamics
facts.text: Validation: Trend significance (Mann–Kendall) and monthly/annual consistency (p-value = 0.0088). Uncertainty: 95% CI of annual growth: +0.6% to +3.0% Limitations: Cloud cover and short summer nights; light is not value added. Status: experimental statistic; confidence high.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Regional growth and convergence
facts.text: Validation: Rank correlation with tropospheric NO₂ (independent source) (Spearman ρ = 0.66). Uncertainty: Class assigned only if |slope| ≥ threshold and p < α; CI of β (robust errors). Limitations: Small units: noise and light blooming between neighbours. Status: experimental statistic; confidence medium.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Light–GDP relationship
facts.text: Validation: Out-of-sample tracking of official growth (correlation / MAE (pp) = -0.54 / 1.7). Uncertainty: 95% CI of the elasticity: -0.19 to 4.11; 80% and 95% prediction intervals. Limitations: Short annual sample; regional GDP is an experimental statistic to be checked against regional accounts. Status: experimental statistic; confidence medium.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Shocks and resilience
facts.text: Validation: Does the trough exceed ordinary variability? (trough (main shock) = -10.4% — no). Uncertainty: Pre-shock month-to-month variability (robust SD); unexplained breaks flagged. Limitations: Shocks hitting poorly lit activities (agriculture, daytime services) are underestimated. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Inequality and electrification
facts.text: Validation: Gap with the World Bank electricity-access rate (mean gap (pp) = -5.6). Uncertainty: Range across radiance thresholds; bootstrap CI of the Gini. Limitations: Proxy of outdoor lighting, not of connection: a connected but dimly lit household looks “in the dark”. Status: experimental statistic; confidence medium.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Industrial zones
facts.text: Validation: Comparison with the reference list (n/a) (precision / recall / F1 = not available). Uncertainty: Per-cluster confidence from the number of strong signals; isolated sites to verify. Limitations: Sentinel-5P (≈ 5 km) and MODIS (1 km) resolution: signals describe a neighbourhood. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Seasonal tourism
facts.text: Validation: Correlation with international tourist arrivals (WDI) (r = -0.28). Uncertainty: p-value per unit; 2020–2021 excluded from the classification. Limitations: Any summer activity (diaspora, second homes, festivals) is captured, not only tourism. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Urbanisation signals
facts.text: Validation: Rank correlation with GHSL built-up area growth (independent source) (Spearman ρ = 0.80). Uncertainty: Persistence required over two years to limit noise; ± 1 pp margin between growth rates before classifying. Limitations: Light measures outdoor lighting, not urbanisation in the administrative sense; blooming widens cities; GHSL population is interpolated between epochs. Status: experimental statistic; confidence high.

facts.title: Method — Method
facts.text: Data: VIIRS DNB monthly (VCMSLCFG) and annual VNL V2, harmonised DMSP–VIIRS, daily Black Marble, GHSL/WorldPop, Sentinel-5P NO₂/SO₂, MODIS LST, World Bank. Cleaning: pixels valid if cf_cvg ≥ 2, unit-month kept if ≥ 80% of pixels observed, spikes replaced, background and gas flares masked.

facts.title: Method — Dynamics
facts.text: Dynamics: robust STL on log(sum of lights), Theil–Sen trend + Mann–Kendall test, year-on-year growth, breaks by piecewise-linear segmentation with a BIC penalty.

facts.title: Method — Regions
facts.text: Regions: robust growth per unit, Growth/Decline class if |slope| ≥ 1%/yr and p < 0.10; β-convergence (robust OLS), σ-convergence, Herfindahl index.

facts.title: Method — GDP
facts.text: GDP: log(NTL) = α + β log(GDP) in levels and growth rates, HAC standard errors, DW/BP/JB diagnostics, out-of-sample tracking; experimental regional GDP allocated by light (γ = 1 and 0.5).

facts.title: Method — Shocks
facts.text: Shocks: trough = largest gap to the 12-month pre-shock level of the seasonally adjusted series, recovery = return to that level; daily Black Marble index (7-day rolling median).

facts.title: Method — Inequality
facts.text: Inequality: population-weighted Gini, Theil (between/within decomposition) and Lorenz; population in the dark = residents of pixels ≥ 5 people below 0.5 nW (sensitivity 0.25/0.5/1).

facts.title: Method — Industry
facts.text: Industry: six signals per pixel (light ≥ 5 nW, light per resident, GHSL non-residential built-up, Sentinel-5P NO₂ and SO₂, MODIS surface heat); pixels with ≥ 3 signals grouped into clusters; typology, confidence from concordant signals, precision/recall validation (official list or OSM).

facts.title: Method — Tourism
facts.text: Tourism: summer excess = log(peak-month light / shoulder-month light); net of the median of comparable units at the same latitude; tourist zone if ≥ +10% and significant over ≥ 3 summers; season index base 100; Ramadan flagged; validation with hotel nights.

facts.title: Method — Urbanisation
facts.text: Urbanisation: annual lit area (pixels ≥ threshold) and its growth (Theil–Sen) compared with population growth (GHSL/WorldPop); newly lit areas (dark in the first 2 years, lit in the last 2), split into electrification of already inhabited areas and new settlements; validation with GHSL BUILT-S built-up growth.

tools.name: search_facts
tools.description: Search the published facts (key messages, methods, limitations, national figures) for those answering a question. Use it first for any general question.

tools.name: rank_units
tools.description: Rank regions (ADM1) or districts (ADM2) by an indicator for the latest year: fastest growth, largest share of population in the dark, etc.

tools.name: unit_profile
tools.description: Full profile of a region or district: latest indicators, light trend, growth class, industrial and tourist zones.

tools.name: compare_units
tools.description: Compare several units (or the country) on an annual indicator between two years: levels, change and compound annual growth rate.

tools.name: make_chart
tools.description: Draw a chart (annual series of an indicator for units, or a ranking bar chart) shown in the conversation.

tools.name: map_action
tools.description: Drive the dashboard's interactive map: show a year, compare two years (swipe), focus on a unit, or show a layer (lights, population in the dark, indicator, industrial clusters, tourist zones).
